data.description:
Goal:
Now that git is gone (K-53), give the docs a real story for how files
move between leaders and from leaders to deploy hosts. Pattern A
(designated store host with sshd + rsync) is the recommended default;
mention B (object storage) and C (direct push) as alternatives. Name
the existing safety nets (K-21 manifest version, K-27 audit log merge)
so multi-leader operators understand why the model is safe under
concurrent writes.

Verification:
1. README gains a "Storing and Syncing" (or "Replication") section, one screen long, that shows:
   - The Pattern A topology: leaders rsync to a store host; hosts rsync from it.
   - One-line concrete example using rsync over ssh.
   - Pattern B / Pattern C named in a few sentences as alternatives.
   - A "Concurrency safety" subsection naming K-21's version check (concurrent writes detected, loser retries) and K-27's audit log merge semantics (union by event UUID).
   - A pointer to the future replication subcommands (K-55..K-57) without preempting their final shape.
2. thimble.md "Peer-to-peer shape" section rewritten to match: file-first, transport-agnostic, store-host as the simple-multi-leader pattern.
3. CONTRIBUTING.md gains a "Running multi-leader" pointer to the README section.
4. No code changes. CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased].

Constraints:
- Knot ref: K-54; depends on K-53.
- Files: README.md, thimble.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md.
- Notes: this is doc-only. The replication primitives the doc references (peers.toml, on-mutate push, heartbeats) are forward references to K-55, K-56, K-57; it's fine to gesture at them as "coming soon" without committing to exact CLI shape.
